best_plan.name: p1
best_plan.rationale: p1 is the best cost-quality trade-off because it filters exactly to taken_3 reviews before any LLM work and then uses a single semantic map that achieved near-perfect aggregation quality, yielding about 0.11666666666666667 positive fraction. Cheaper models like p2, p3, and p5 were slightly less expensive but materially worse on quality, so their savings were not worth the error.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "taken_3")
pipeline.sem_map(
    [{"name": "is_positive", "type": bool, "description": "Whether the review text expresses an overall positive opinion of the movie."}],
    model=pz.Model.GPT_4_1_MINI,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.groupby([], ["average"], ["is_positive"])
pipeline.project(["average(is_positive)"])
pipeline

cost_model_explanation: The cost model consistently favored plans that pushed the exact idx filter before the semantic operator, since that reduced the LLM workload to 120 reviews instead of the full table. Among single-semantic-pass plans, the cheaper models were p3 and p2, but observed quality dropped substantially; GPT-4.1 Mini cost more than those lightweight options but delivered the best accuracy, making it the best overall choice.
